515	Milne III Theorem 5.1(a) (the proof uses dimension count plus the
516	Riemann–Roch identification of the generic fibre as a single point on
517	a curve of genus `g`).

519	Blueprint reference: `lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian` (Milne,
520	*Abelian Varieties*, Theorem III.5.1(a), p. 101). -/

546	/-! ## §5. Descent through the birational quotient
547	
548	The final auxiliary lemma packages the two-step descent that promotes
549	`Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` (after passing through the birational morphism
550	`f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`) to a regular morphism
551	`ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`. The descent is a rational map
552	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A` on the dense open of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` on which
553	`f^{(g)}` is an isomorphism, then promoted to a regular morphism via
554	Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (the sibling `Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`).
555	This is the only step of the proof that uses the rational-map extension.
556	
557	Blueprint reference: `lem:descent_through_birational_sigma` (Milne's
558	proof of III.6.1, p. 104, "It therefore defines a rational map
559	`ψ : J → A`, which (I 3.2) shows to be a regular map"). -/
560	
561	/-- **Descent of `Sym^g φ` to a regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`.**
562	
563	There is a *unique* regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` such that
564	`symmetricPowerAVMap C (genus C) φ = symmetricPowerToJacobian C P₀ (genus C) ≫ ψ`
565	(equivalently, `ψ` is the unique regular extension of the rational map
566	`Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1} : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`).
567	
568	The rational map is constructed on the dense open `V ⊆ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
569	where `f^{(g)}` is an isomorphism, then promoted to a regular morphism
570	on all of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` via Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (sibling
571	`Scheme.RationalMap.extend_to_av` in
572	`Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`). Uniqueness is the
573	standard reduced-and-separated agreement principle: two regular
574	morphisms `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` agreeing on a dense open are equal.
575	
576	**Not yet proved — but the extension half is done.** The gap is now precisely
577	one thing: the *birationality data*. Specifically:
578	
579	* `Scheme.RationalMap.exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open`
580	  (`Albanese/DenseOpenDescent.lean`) says that given **any** dense open
581	  `V ⊆ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` and **any** morphism `h : V ⟶ A` compatible with the
582	  structure maps, there is a unique `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` with `V.ι ≫ ψ = h`.
583	  It is proved and axiom-clean, resting on `extend_to_av` (Milne Theorem 3.2),
584	  itself unconditional since Milne Lemma 3.3 closed.
585	
586	So no further extension, properness or agreement argument is needed here. What
587	remains is to *produce* `V` and `h`: the dense open of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` over which
588	`f^{(g)}` admits a section, and that section composed with `Sym^g φ`. That needs
589	(i) `Sym^g C` and `f^{(g)}` to exist at all, and (ii) Milne III Theorem 5.1(a)'s
590	birationality in a usable form — mathlib at this pin has no API for inverting a
591	birational morphism on a dense open (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Birational/`
592	supplies `IsDominant`, not an inverse). -/

640	/-! ## §6. The Albanese universal property — headline theorem
641	
642	The headline result of the chapter: for every pointed morphism
643	`φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety `A` with `φ(P₀) = η_A`, there
644	exists a unique regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` such that
645	`φ = ψ ∘ ι_{P₀}`. The proof follows Milne Proposition III.6.1
646	verbatim, using the four sub-lemmas above plus Milne Theorem I.3.2
647	(`extend_to_av`) and Corollary I.1.2 (a `thm:rigidity_lemma`
648	consequence).
649	
650	Blueprint reference: `thm:albanese_universal_property` (Milne,
651	*Abelian Varieties*, Proposition III.6.1, p. 104). -/
652	
653	/-- **Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` — Milne III §6
654	Proposition 6.1.**
655	
656	For a complete nonsingular curve `C` of genus `g > 0` over an
657	algebraically closed field `k̄`, a marked `k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, and
658	every pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety `A` with
659	`φ(P₀) = η_A`, there exists a *unique* regular morphism
660	`ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` such that `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ`.
661	
662	Proof sketch (Milne III.6.1):
663	1. **Symmetrisation.** `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` is
664	   `S_g`-symmetric (`A` commutative), so factors through
665	   `Sym^g C` as `Sym^g φ` (`lem:symmetric_product_av_map`).
666	2. **Descent to a regular morphism on `J`.** The birational morphism
667	   `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (`lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian`)
668	   exhibits `Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1}` as a rational map
669	   `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, which by Milne Theorem I.3.2 extends uniquely to
670	   a regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`
671	   (`lem:descent_through_birational_sigma`).
672	3. **Factorisation `ψ ∘ ι_{P₀} = φ`.** Use Milne's identification of
673	   `ι_{P₀}` with the composite `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by
674	   `f^{(g)}`; together with `φ(P₀) = η_A` and the additive structure
675	   of `A`, this gives `ψ(ι_{P₀}(Q)) = φ(Q)` on `k̄`-points, hence
676	   globally by the reduced-and-separated agreement principle.
677	4. **Homomorphism property.** `ψ` sends `η_J = ι_{P₀}(P₀)` to
678	   `φ(P₀) = η_A`, so by Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a `thm:rigidity_lemma`
679	   consequence) it is a homomorphism of group schemes.
680	5. **Uniqueness.** Two homomorphisms `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` with the same
681	   restriction to `ι_{P₀}(C)` agree on the `g`-fold sum
682	   `ι_{P₀}(C) + ⋯ + ι_{P₀}(C) = Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (since `f^{(g)}` is
683	   surjective), hence are equal.
684	
685	The statement asserts only the existence and uniqueness of the factoring
686	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` (matching the project's `IsAlbanese`
687	convention in `Jacobian.lean`); the group-homomorphism property is implicit
688	in the construction, by Milne Corollary I.1.2 (registered in
689	`chap:AbelianVarietyRigidity`).

9	/-!
10	# The symmetric power as an *interface*, and the two maps it produces
11	
12	Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
13	Proposition 6.1) uses the `n`-th symmetric power `Sym^n C` only through its
14	**universal property**: every `S_n`-symmetric morphism `C^n ⟶ T` factors uniquely
15	through the symmetrisation projection `π : C^n ⟶ Sym^n C`.
16	
17	At this Mathlib pin the *object* `Sym^n C` does not exist for a proper curve — there is no
18	quotient of a scheme by a finite group action, and mathlib's `SymmetricPower` is for
19	modules. (The `analogies/m3-route-audit.md` figure of 2400–3800 lines priced Milne's
20	affine-and-glue route; `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` later reduced the obligation to one
21	`HasColimit` instance and discharged the affine half outright. Read that file before
22	budgeting anything from this paragraph.) Writing `Sym^n C := sorry` makes every downstream
23	equation a statement
24	about a junk term, which is why `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` keeps its obligations
25	unproved rather than discharging them against a meaningless definition.
26	
27	This file takes the other route: it **names the interface** as a structure
28	`SymPowData C n`, and then proves, unconditionally, everything Milne's argument
29	derives from it. The missing geometry is isolated in exactly one place — inhabiting
30	`SymPowData` — and nothing downstream is a statement about `sorry`.

32	## What is proved here (no `sorry`, nothing conditional on unproved statements)
33	
34	* `SymPowData.symAVMap` — Milne's `Sym^n φ`. Given `φ : C ⟶ A` into a *commutative*
35	  monoid object, the `n`-fold sum `powSum n φ` is `S_n`-symmetric
36	  (`MonObj.powSum_perm`, already proved), so the interface descends it. This is the
37	  content of `lem:symmetric_product_av_map`, and it is a construction, not a
38	  hypothesis.
39	* `SymPowData.proj_comp_symAVMap` / `SymPowData.symAVMap_unique` — its defining
40	  equation and uniqueness.
41	* `MonObj.basePointShift` — the morphism `Q ↦ (P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)` placing `Q` in a
42	  designated slot `i₀` and the basepoint elsewhere. Milne's `Q ↦ Q + (n−1) P₀`
43	  factors through it.
44	* `MonObj.basePointShift_comp_powSum` — **the computation that makes the backward
45	  direction of the Albanese connector work**: for a *pointed* `φ` (`P₀ ≫ φ = η[A]`),
46	
47	  `basePointShift P₀ i₀ ≫ powSum n φ = φ`,
48	
49	  because `φ(Q) + φ(P₀) + ⋯ + φ(P₀) = φ(Q) + η + ⋯ + η = φ(Q)`. In the hom-monoid
50	  this is `Finset.prod_ite_eq`; the geometry evaporates exactly as it does in
51	  `GrpObjFoldSum.lean`.
52	* `symPowDataOne` and `symPowDataOne_proj_perm` — **an inhabitant of the interface
53	  *together with* the symmetry hypothesis**: `Sym^1 C = C`. See the warning below for
54	  why both halves are needed and what they do and do not show.
55	
56	## What non-vacuity does and does not mean here — read this before citing it
57	
58	`SymPowData C n` **on its own is trivially inhabited for every `n`** — and the witness
59	is recorded below as `symPowDataTrivial` rather than left as a remark, so that nobody
60	has to rediscover it:
61	
62	```
63	carrier := C^n,  proj := 𝟙,  desc := fun h _ => ⟨h, Category.id_comp h, …⟩
64	```
65	
66	With `proj = 𝟙` the universal property degenerates to `∃! u, 𝟙 ≫ u = h`. So the bare
67	structure is nearly free, and exhibiting *some* `SymPowData` proves nothing.
68	
69	What the downstream theorems actually quantify over is the **pair**
70	`(D, hproj)`, where `hproj : ∀ σ, permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj` says the projection
71	is genuinely symmetric. The `proj := 𝟙` trick fails that whenever `permAut C σ ≠ 𝟙`, which
72	for `n ≥ 2` holds as soon as `C` has two distinct global points — the case of interest, and
73	proved in `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` (`permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points`). It is *not*
74	automatic from `n ≥ 2` alone: at a **terminal** `C` the trivial datum does satisfy `hproj`
75	at every `n` (`permAut_eq_id_of_isTerminal`), so an unqualified "fails for `n ≥ 2`" is
76	false. So the pair is the meaningful object away from that degenerate case, and this file
77	witnesses it for `n = 1`: `symPowDataOne` plus `symPowDataOne_proj_perm`.
78	
79	Two honest caveats about that witness:
80	
81	* `n = 1` is the case where the *interesting* step degenerates. The forward direction
82	  of the connector (`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`) uses that `ψ` is a homomorphism
83	  to move it through a `g`-fold product; a 1-fold product has one factor, so at
84	  `n = 1` that step is mere associativity. The general-`n` theorem is the real one —
85	  do not cite `n = 1` as evidence that the group law is exercised.
86	* Consequently, "the interface is inhabited" should be read as *the hypotheses are
87	  consistent and the statements are not about nothing*, not as *the hard case is
88	  covered*.
89	
90	## What is *not* here — but see `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` first
91	
92	**This section is superseded in part (2026-07-28).** It said `SymPowData C n` for `n ≥ 2`

138	/-! ## §1. The interface
139	
140	`SymPowData C n` is exactly the data Milne's proof uses: a scheme, a symmetrisation
141	projection from `C^n`, and the universal property for `S_n`-symmetric morphisms. The
142	symmetry hypothesis is phrased with `MonObj.permAut` (`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`),
143	the factor-permuting automorphism of `C^n`. -/
144	
145	/-- **The universal property of the `n`-th symmetric power, as data.**
146	
147	A `SymPowData C n` is a `carrier` (morally `Sym^n C`) together with a symmetrisation
148	morphism `proj : C^n ⟶ carrier` through which *every* `S_n`-symmetric morphism out of
149	`C^n` factors uniquely.
150	
151	This is the interface, not the construction: see `symPowDataOne` for the case `n = 1`,
152	and the module header for why the general case is a separate subproject. -/
153	structure SymPowData (C : K) (n : ℕ) where
154	  /-- The underlying object, morally `Sym^n C`. -/
155	  carrier : K
156	  /-- The symmetrisation projection `π : C^n ⟶ Sym^n C`. -/
157	  proj : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ carrier
158	  /-- **The universal property.** Every `S_n`-symmetric morphism `C^n ⟶ T` factors
159	  uniquely through `proj`. -/
160	  desc : ∀ {T : K} (h : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ T),
161	    (∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ h = h) →
162	    ∃! u : carrier ⟶ T, proj ≫ u = h
163	
164	namespace SymPowData
165	
166	variable {C : K} {n : ℕ}
167	
168	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
169	/-- Uniqueness of a factorisation through `proj`, in the form used at call sites:
170	two morphisms out of the carrier that agree after `proj` are equal.
171	
172	Note that no symmetry hypothesis is needed: if `u₁` and `u₂` both factor `h` then
173	`h` *is* symmetric (being `proj ≫ u₁` with `proj` symmetric would be the argument,
174	but here we get it more cheaply — apply `desc` to `proj ≫ u₁`, whose symmetry follows
175	from that of `proj` composed with anything). We therefore take the symmetry of
176	`proj` itself as the input. -/
177	theorem hom_ext_of_proj (D : SymPowData C n) {T : K} {u₁ u₂ : D.carrier ⟶ T}
178	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
179	    (h : D.proj ≫ u₁ = D.proj ≫ u₂) : u₁ = u₂ := by
180	  obtain ⟨u, -, huniq⟩ := D.desc (D.proj ≫ u₁) (fun σ => by rw [← Category.assoc, hproj])
181	  rw [huniq u₁ rfl, huniq u₂ h.symm]
182	
183	section SymAVMap
184	
185	variable [BraidedCategory K]
186	
187	/-- **Milne's `Sym^n φ`.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative monoid object, the
188	`n`-fold sum `(P₁,…,P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_n)` is `S_n`-symmetric
189	(`MonObj.powSum_perm` — Milne's "clearly this is symmetric"), so the interface
190	descends it to `Sym^n C ⟶ A`.
191	
192	This is `lem:symmetric_product_av_map`: a *construction* from the interface, with no
193	further geometric input. -/
194	noncomputable def symAVMap {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
195	    (D : SymPowData C n) (φ : C ⟶ A) : D.carrier ⟶ A :=
196	  (D.desc (MonObj.powSum n φ) (fun σ => MonObj.powSum_perm n φ σ)).choose
197	
198	/-- The defining equation of `Sym^n φ`: it restores the `n`-fold sum along `proj`. -/
199	@[reassoc]
200	theorem proj_comp_symAVMap {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
201	    (D : SymPowData C n) (φ : C ⟶ A) :
202	    D.proj ≫ D.symAVMap φ = MonObj.powSum n φ :=
203	  (D.desc (MonObj.powSum n φ) (fun σ => MonObj.powSum_perm n φ σ)).choose_spec.1
204	
205	/-- `Sym^n φ` is the *unique* morphism restoring the `n`-fold sum along `proj`. -/
206	theorem symAVMap_unique {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
207	    (D : SymPowData C n) (φ : C ⟶ A) (u : D.carrier ⟶ A)
208	    (hu : D.proj ≫ u = MonObj.powSum n φ) : u = D.symAVMap φ :=
209	  (D.desc (MonObj.powSum n φ) (fun σ => MonObj.powSum_perm n φ σ)).choose_spec.2 u hu
210	
211	end SymAVMap
212	
213	end SymPowData

215	/-! ## §2. Milne's `Q ↦ Q + (n − 1) P₀`, and why it collapses the sum
216	
217	The backward direction of the Albanese connector restricts the symmetric-power
218	equation along `Q ↦ (Q, P₀, …, P₀)`. The whole force of that step is the following
219	computation in the hom-monoid: summing `φ` over such a tuple gives
220	`φ(Q) + φ(P₀) + ⋯ + φ(P₀)`, and a *pointed* `φ` kills every term but the first. -/
221	
222	namespace MonObj
223	
224	variable {C : K}
225	
226	/-- **The basepoint shift `Q ↦ (P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)`**, placing `Q` in the designated
227	slot `i₀` and the basepoint `P₀ : 𝟙_ ⟶ C` in every other slot.
228	
229	Composed with the symmetrisation projection this is Milne's
230	`Q ↦ Q + (n − 1) P₀ : C ⟶ Sym^n C`. -/
231	noncomputable def basePointShift (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) {n : ℕ} (i₀ : Fin n) :
232	    C ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) :=
233	  Pi.lift (fun i => if i = i₀ then 𝟙 C else toUnit C ≫ P0)
234	
235	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
236	theorem basePointShift_π (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) {n : ℕ} (i₀ i : Fin n) :
237	    basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i
238	      = if i = i₀ then 𝟙 C else toUnit C ≫ P0 := by
239	  simp only [basePointShift, Pi.lift_π]
240	
241	section Collapse
242	
243	variable [BraidedCategory K]
244	
245	/-- **The collapse computation.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative monoid object
246	which is *pointed* at `P₀` (`P₀ ≫ φ = η[A]`), summing `φ` over the tuple
247	`(P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)` returns `φ` itself:
248	
249	`basePointShift P₀ i₀ ≫ powSum n φ = φ`.
250	
251	Every slot other than `i₀` contributes `toUnit ≫ P₀ ≫ φ = toUnit ≫ η[A] = 1`, the
252	identity of the hom-monoid, so the product collapses to the single factor at `i₀`
253	(`Finset.prod_ite_eq`). This is the entire content of Milne's "restrict along
254	`Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` and use `φ(P₀) = η_A`". -/
255	theorem basePointShift_comp_powSum {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
256	    (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) {n : ℕ} (i₀ : Fin n) (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A]) :
257	    basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ powSum n φ = φ := by
258	  classical
259	  rw [comp_powSum]
260	  have hterm : ∀ i : Fin n,
261	      basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ
262	        = if i₀ = i then φ else 1 := by
263	    intro i
264	    rw [← Category.assoc, basePointShift_π]
265	    by_cases h : i = i₀
266	    · subst h; simp
267	    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg (fun hc => h hc.symm), Category.assoc, hφ, ← Hom.one_def]
268	  rw [Finset.prod_congr rfl (fun i _ => hterm i), Finset.prod_ite_eq]
269	  simp
270	
271	end Collapse
272	
273	end MonObj

276	
277	For `n = 1` the symmetric group is trivial, `C^1 ⟶ C` is an isomorphism, and the
278	universal property is immediate. Both halves of the meaningful object are supplied: the
279	datum `symPowDataOne` and the symmetry `symPowDataOne_proj_perm`.
280	
281	As the module header warns, the bare structure `SymPowData C n` is trivially inhabited
282	for every `n` (take `proj := 𝟙`), so it is the **pair** with `hproj` that carries

286	morphism out of `C^1` — symmetric or not, since `S_1` is trivial — factors uniquely

292	noncomputable def symPowDataOne (C : K) : SymPowData C 1 where
293	  carrier := C
294	  proj := Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0
295	  desc := fun {T} h _ => by
296	    -- `Pi.lift (fun _ => 𝟙 C)` is a two-sided inverse of the single projection.
297	    have hsec : Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C)) ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 = 𝟙 C := by
298	      rw [Pi.lift_π]
299	    have hret : Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 ≫ Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C))
300	        = 𝟙 (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin 1 => C)) := by
301	      apply Pi.hom_ext
302	      intro b
303	      have hb : b = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
304	      subst hb
305	      rw [Category.assoc, Pi.lift_π, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
306	    refine ⟨Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C)) ≫ h, ?_, ?_⟩
307	    · change Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 ≫ Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C)) ≫ h = h
308	      rw [← Category.assoc, hret, Category.id_comp]
309	    · intro u hu
310	      rw [← hu, ← Category.assoc, hsec, Category.id_comp]
311	
312	/-- **The trivial witness — kept deliberately, as the acceptance test for this file.**
313	
314	`SymPowData C n` is inhabited for *every* `n` by taking `proj := 𝟙`, which makes the
315	universal property vacuous. This declaration exists so that the limitation is a checked
316	fact in the tree rather than a remark someone might doubt or forget.

332	noncomputable def symPowDataTrivial (C : K) (n : ℕ) : SymPowData C n where
333	  carrier := ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)
334	  proj := 𝟙 _
335	  desc := fun {_} h _ => ⟨h, Category.id_comp h, fun _ hu => by simpa using hu⟩

22	
23	* **no `SymPowData` argument** — the symmetric power is `symPowOfColimit C g`;
24	* **no `hproj` argument** — the symmetry is discharged internally by
25	  `symPowOfColimit_proj_perm`, i.e. by `colimit.w`;

9	/-!
10	# The `n`-fold tensor power is the `n`-ary coproduct of algebras
11	
12	`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean` lists four inputs a `Scheme.GlueData` for `Sym^n C`
13	needs. Item 3 is the comparison
14	
15	> the `n`-ary coproduct of `R`-algebras **is** the `n`-fold tensor power `⨂[R] i, A i`,
16	
17	which two previous sessions on this leg recorded as absent from mathlib and unbuilt in AJC,
18	with the consequence that `SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra` (whose diagram is built
19	from the `n`-ary **coproduct** in `Under k`) and the whole `PiTensorProduct` layer
20	(`Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean`, `SymPowInvariants*.lean`) were provably *about different
21	objects*. That mismatch is what this file removes.
22	
23	## What was actually missing, and what was not
24	
25	Mathlib has the **binary** case as a pushout (`CommRingCat.pushoutCoconeIsColimit`,
26	`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Ring/Constructions.lean`) and nothing `n`-ary. But it turns out that
27	*both halves of the `n`-ary universal property are already in mathlib*, unbundled and not
28	labelled as a colimit:
29	
30	* **uniqueness** is `PiTensorProduct.algHom_ext` — two algebra maps out of a finite tensor
31	  power agree as soon as they agree on each `PiTensorProduct.singleAlgHom i`, the inclusion
32	  `a ↦ 1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ 1`. That is exactly `Cofan.IsColimit`'s uniqueness clause;
33	* **existence** is one application of `PiTensorProduct.liftAlgHom` to the multilinear map
34	  `x ↦ ∏ i, f i (x i)`, and is `coprodLift` below.
35	
36	So the honest description of item 3 is not "mathlib lacks the `n`-ary comparison" but "mathlib
37	has it in pieces, under names that do not mention colimits". The only mathematical content
38	supplied here is the multilinearity of `x ↦ ∏ i, f i (x i)`, which is
39	`Finset.prod_update_of_mem` three times.
40	
41	**Where commutativity is load-bearing.** `coprodLift` needs the target `S` to be
42	*commutative*: the product `∏ i, f i (x i)` must be independent of the order of the factors,
43	and multiplicativity `f (x * y) = f x * f y` is `Finset.prod_mul_distrib`. This is why the
44	statement is about the coproduct in **commutative** algebras — which is the category the
45	affine symmetric power lives in — and not a coproduct in all `R`-algebras, where the tensor
46	power is *not* the coproduct. A reader coming from the noncommutative case should not read
47	this file as more general than it is.
48	
49	## Main results
50	
51	* `PiTensorProduct.coprodLift` — the lift of a family `f : ∀ i, A i →ₐ[R] S` into a
52	  commutative `S`, together with `coprodLift_tprod` and
53	  `coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom` (its defining equation).
54	* `PiTensorProduct.existsUnique_coprodLift` — the `n`-ary coproduct universal property as a
55	  single `∃!` statement: this is the form a colimit consumer wants.
56	* `PiTensorProduct.coprodLift_permAlgHom` — **the equivariance that item 3 actually asks
57	  for**, and the reason this file imports `SymPowTensorAction`: the comparison intertwines
58	  the factor-permutation action `permAlgHom` on the tensor power with *reindexing the family*.
59	  Without it the identification would be an isomorphism of objects that does not respect the
60	  `S_n`-actions, and so would say nothing about symmetric powers (the failure mode recorded
61	  in this leg's memory as "groups agree ≠ maps agree").
62	
63	## What this does *not* close
64	
65	Item 3 of the four-item bill, only. In particular:
66	
67	* it does **not** build the `Under k`-valued or `CommRingCat`-valued cofan and prove
68	  `IsColimit` of it. The algebra-level `∃!` is the mathematical content; crossing into
69	  `(Under k)ᵒᵖ` is bookkeeping this file deliberately leaves to its consumer, since
70	  `SymPowColimit`'s §5 caveat about which category is which is exactly where a previous
71	  session went wrong;
72	* `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` for the curve remains open, and `AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six
73	  sorries are unchanged.
74	
75	## References
76	
77	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1, p. 94 (the affine symmetric power
78	`(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`). Mathlib's binary comparison:
79	`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Ring/Constructions.lean`.
80	-/

92	variable {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} {A : ι → Type w} {S : Type*}
93	  [CommRing R] [∀ i, CommRing (A i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (A i)] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
94	
95	section Mk
96	
97	variable [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
98	
99	omit [Fintype ι] in
100	/-- **Postcomposing a family of algebra maps commutes with `Function.update`.** The one
101	bookkeeping fact behind multilinearity of `x ↦ ∏ i, f i (x i)`: changing the `i`-th entry of
102	the tuple changes the `i`-th factor of the product and nothing else. -/
103	private theorem comp_update (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) (x : ∀ i, A i) (i : ι) (v : A i) :
104	    (fun j => f j (Function.update x i v j))
105	      = Function.update (fun j => f j (x j)) i (f i v) := by
106	  funext j
107	  by_cases hj : j = i
108	  · subst hj; simp
109	  · simp [Function.update_of_ne hj]
110	
111	/-- **The multilinear map underlying the coproduct lift**, `x ↦ ∏ i, f i (x i)`.
112	
113	Both multilinearity clauses are `comp_update` followed by `Finset.prod_update_of_mem`, which
114	isolates the `i`-th factor; then `map_add` / `map_smul` of `f i` and distributivity. -/
115	noncomputable def coprodMultilinear (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) :
116	    MultilinearMap R A S :=
117	  MultilinearMap.mk (fun x => ∏ i, f i (x i))
118	    (by
119	      intro _ x i a b
120	      rw [comp_update f x i (a + b), comp_update f x i a, comp_update f x i b,
121	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i),
122	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i),
123	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i), map_add, add_mul])
124	    (by
125	      intro _ x i c a
126	      rw [comp_update f x i (c • a), comp_update f x i a,
127	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i),
128	        Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i), map_smul, smul_mul_assoc])
129	
130	omit [DecidableEq ι] in
131	@[simp]
132	theorem coprodMultilinear_apply (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) (x : ∀ i, A i) :
133	    coprodMultilinear f x = ∏ i, f i (x i) := rfl
134	
135	/-- **The coproduct lift.** A family of algebra maps `f i : A i →ₐ[R] S` into a
136	*commutative* `S` induces an algebra map out of the tensor power, sending
137	`a_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a_n` to `f_1(a_1) ⋯ f_n(a_n)`.
138	
139	Unitality is `∏ i, f i 1 = 1`; multiplicativity is `Finset.prod_mul_distrib`, and **this is
140	where commutativity of `S` is used** — see the module header. -/
141	noncomputable def coprodLift (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) :
142	    (⨂[R] i, A i) →ₐ[R] S :=
143	  liftAlgHom (coprodMultilinear f)
144	    (by simp)
145	    (by
146	      intro x y
147	      simp only [coprodMultilinear_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, Finset.prod_mul_distrib])
148	
149	omit [DecidableEq ι] in
150	@[simp]
151	theorem coprodLift_tprod (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) (x : ∀ i, A i) :
152	    coprodLift f (tprod R x) = ∏ i, f i (x i) := by
153	  simp [coprodLift]
154	
155	/-- **The defining equation of the coproduct lift.** Precomposing with the `i`-th structural
156	inclusion `singleAlgHom i` recovers `f i`: every factor other than the `i`-th contributes
157	`f j 1 = 1`. -/
158	theorem coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) (i : ι) :
159	    (coprodLift f).comp (singleAlgHom i) = f i := by
160	  ext a
161	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, singleAlgHom_apply, coprodLift_tprod]
162	  have h : (fun j => f j (MonoidHom.mulSingle A i a j))
163	      = Function.update (fun _ => (1 : S)) i (f i a) := by
164	    funext j
165	    by_cases hj : j = i
166	    · subst hj; simp
167	    · simp [Function.update_of_ne hj, Pi.mulSingle_eq_of_ne hj]
168	  rw [h, Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i)]
169	  simp
170	
171	set_option linter.unusedFintypeInType false in
172	/-- **The `n`-ary coproduct universal property of the tensor power, as one statement.**
173	
174	For a finite family of commutative `R`-algebras `A i` and a commutative `R`-algebra `S`,
175	algebra maps out of `⨂[R] i, A i` correspond to families of algebra maps out of the `A i`:
176	there is a *unique* `u` with `u ∘ singleAlgHom i = f i` for every `i`.
177	
178	This is the shape a `Cofan.IsColimit` consumer wants. Existence is `coprodLift`; uniqueness
179	is mathlib's `algHom_ext`, which is the coproduct uniqueness clause under another name.
180	
181	The `[Fintype ι]` binder does not appear in the statement's *type* (the linter says so) but is
182	load-bearing in the proof: `coprodLift`'s product `∏ i, f i (x i)` needs it. `Finite` would do
183	after `Fintype.ofFinite`, but then the witness would not be syntactically `coprodLift f`, which
184	is what call sites rewrite with. -/
185	theorem existsUnique_coprodLift (f : (i : ι) → (A i →ₐ[R] S)) :
186	    ∃! u : (⨂[R] i, A i) →ₐ[R] S, ∀ i, u.comp (singleAlgHom i) = f i :=
187	  ⟨coprodLift f, coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom f,
188	    fun _ hu => algHom_ext fun i => (hu i).trans (coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom f i).symm⟩
189	
190	end Mk
191	
192	/-! ### Equivariance: the comparison respects the `S_n`-actions
193	
194	The identification above is an isomorphism of *objects*. For the symmetric power it must also
195	match the actions on the two sides — otherwise it is the "groups agree but the maps do not"
196	failure this project has hit before, and it would license nothing about `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`.
197	
198	The statement is the natural one: permuting the factors of the tensor power and then lifting
199	`f` is the same as lifting the *reindexed* family. Since all the `A i` are the same algebra
200	`A` in the symmetric-power application, "reindexed family" is just `f ∘ e`. -/
201	
202	section Equivariance
203	
204	-- `A'` must live in the *ring's* universe `u`: `SymPowTensorAction.permAlgHom` is stated with
205	-- `(R : Type u) (A : Type u)`, so a `Type w` algebra cannot be permuted by it. Matching the
206	-- binder here rather than generalising `permAlgHom` keeps this file additive over that one.
207	-- No `DecidableEq ι`: the proof opens with `classical`, so it would be an unused binder in the
208	-- statement (and the linter rightly rejects it).
209	variable {A' : Type u} [CommRing A'] [Algebra R A'] [Fintype ι]
210	
211	/-- **The comparison is equivariant.** For a constant family `A' i = A'`, permuting the
212	tensor factors along `e` and then lifting `f` agrees with lifting the family reindexed along
213	`e⁻¹`:
214	
215	`coprodLift f ∘ permAlgHom e = coprodLift (f ∘ e⁻¹)`.
216	
217	**Read the variance, and do not guess it.** The first draft of this lemma stated `f ∘ e` on
218	the right and was *false*: the residual goal was `f (e⁻¹ i) a = f (e i) a`, which holds only
219	at an involution. On generators, `permAlgHom e` sends `tprod x` to `tprod (x ∘ e)`, so the
220	lift becomes `∏ i, f i (x (e i))`; reindexing `j = e i` turns that into
221	`∏ j, f (e⁻¹ j) (x j)`, which is the lift of `f ∘ e⁻¹`. The inverse here is the *same*
222	`permAlgHom` anti-homomorphism bookkeeping that `SymPowTensorAction.permAlgHom_comp` records
223	and that `permMulSemiringAction` absorbs by acting through `σ⁻¹`.
224	
225	This is the clause that makes the identification usable for symmetric powers rather than
226	merely true: without it the two sides carry unrelated `S_n`-actions, and an isomorphism of
227	objects alone licenses nothing about `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`. -/
228	theorem coprodLift_permAlgHom (f : ι → (A' →ₐ[R] S)) (e : Equiv.Perm ι) :
229	    (coprodLift (A := fun _ : ι => A') f).comp (permAlgHom R A' e)
230	      = coprodLift (A := fun _ : ι => A') (fun i => f (e.symm i)) := by
231	  classical
232	  refine algHom_ext fun i => ?_
233	  ext a
234	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.comp_apply, singleAlgHom_apply, permAlgHom_tprod,
235	    coprodLift_tprod, AlgHom.comp_apply, singleAlgHom_apply, coprodLift_tprod]
236	  -- Both sides are a product with a single nontrivial factor; identify which slot.
237	  have hl : (fun j => f j (MonoidHom.mulSingle (fun _ : ι => A') i a (e j)))
238	      = Function.update (fun _ => (1 : S)) (e.symm i) (f (e.symm i) a) := by
239	    funext j
240	    by_cases hj : j = e.symm i
241	    · subst hj; simp
242	    · have hne : e j ≠ i := fun hc => hj (by rw [← hc, Equiv.symm_apply_apply])
243	      simp [Function.update_of_ne hj, Pi.mulSingle_eq_of_ne hne]
244	  have hr : (fun j => f (e.symm j) (MonoidHom.mulSingle (fun _ : ι => A') i a j))
245	      = Function.update (fun _ => (1 : S)) i (f (e.symm i) a) := by
246	    funext j
247	    by_cases hj : j = i
248	    · subst hj; simp
249	    · simp [Function.update_of_ne hj, Pi.mulSingle_eq_of_ne hj]
250	  rw [hl, hr, Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _),
251	    Finset.prod_update_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i)]
252	  simp
253	
254	omit [Fintype ι] in
255	/-- **The action on the coprojections: permuting factors relabels the inclusions.**
256	
257	`permAlgHom e ∘ singleAlgHom i = singleAlgHom (e⁻¹ i)`.
258	
259	This is the statement that matches the two `S_n`-actions *at the level of the coproduct
260	structure*, and it is the one "matching the permutation action to `permAlgHom`" really asks
261	for: `coprodLift_permAlgHom` above relates the lift to itself under reindexing, with both
262	sides inside `PiTensorProduct`, whereas this one says how the action moves the `i`-th
263	coprojection — the datum a cofan is built from.
264	
265	Note it carries `e⁻¹`, independently confirming the variance of `coprodLift_permAlgHom`:
266	`permAlgHom e` sends `tprod x` to `tprod (x ∘ e)`, so the tuple `mulSingle i a` is hit at the
267	slot `j` with `e j = i`. -/
268	theorem permAlgHom_comp_singleAlgHom [DecidableEq ι] (e : Equiv.Perm ι) (i : ι) :
269	    (permAlgHom R A' e).comp (singleAlgHom (R := R) (A := fun _ : ι => A') i)
270	      = singleAlgHom (R := R) (A := fun _ : ι => A') (e.symm i) := by
271	  classical
272	  ext a
273	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, singleAlgHom_apply, permAlgHom_tprod, singleAlgHom_apply]
274	  congr 1
275	  funext j
276	  by_cases hj : j = e.symm i
277	  · subst hj; simp
278	  · have hne : e j ≠ i := fun hc => hj (by rw [← hc, Equiv.symm_apply_apply])
279	    simp [Pi.mulSingle_eq_of_ne hj, Pi.mulSingle_eq_of_ne hne]

281	end Equivariance

9	/-!
10	# The invariants as a limit **over the base**: closing the category mismatch
11	
12	`Albanese/SymPowInvariants.lean` proved that the invariant subring is the limit of a group
13	action — in `CommRingCat`, with no base ring. Its §4 then flagged, as the third of three open
14	items, that this is **the wrong category** for the consumer:
15	
16	> **The category.** `SymPowColimit`'s affine statement is over `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`; everything here
17	> is over `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`. No declaration bridges them, so nothing in that file can consume
18	> anything in this one.
19	
20	That item is closed here, and closed by *restating rather than bridging* — which turned out
21	to be the cheaper route. Rather than transporting the `CommRingCat` limit across
22	`Over.opEquivOpUnder`, the cone is rebuilt directly in `Under k`: the invariant
23	**subalgebra** `A^G` is already a `k`-algebra, so it is an object of `Under k` on the nose,
24	and the limit proof is the `CommRingCat` one with `(Under.forget k).map_injective` inserted
25	before each `hom_ext`. No transport, no `eqToHom`, no defeq wall.
26	
27	## Main results
28	
29	* `actionDiagramUnder` — the action as a diagram in `Under k`. Well-defined exactly because
30	  the action fixes the base: that is `[SMulCommClass G k A]`, and the proof is
31	  `algebraMap r = r • 1` followed by `smul_comm`.
32	* `fixedUnder` — `A^G` as an object of `Under k`, i.e. as a `k`-algebra.
33	* `fixedConeUnderIsLimit` — **the identification over the base**: the cone with vertex `A^G`
34	  is a limit cone in `Under k`.
35	* `hasLimit_actionDiagramUnder`, `fixedCoconeUnderIsColimitOp`,
36	  `hasColimit_actionDiagramUnder_op` — the `HasLimit` form and the dual, in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`,
37	  which is the variance and the category of `SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra`.
38	* `hasColimit_actionDiagramUnder_op_symTensorPow` — the whole stack at Milne's ring: the
39	  `S_n`-action on `A^{⊗ n}` from `SymPowTensorAction`, quotiented over `k`.
40	* `hasColimit_singleObj_of_op` / `invEquivalence_comp_op_map` — the **index-category** step,
41	  which an earlier draft of this file wrongly treated as absent: `Functor.op` gives a diagram
42	  over `(SingleObj G)ᵒᵖ`, not over `SingleObj G`, and the transport is `Groupoid.invEquivalence`
43	  with the reindexing being `σ ↦ σ⁻¹` on the nose.
44	
45	## What the hypothesis `[SMulCommClass G k A]` is, and why it is not a weakening
46	
47	`SymPowInvariants` assumed nothing beyond a `MulSemiringAction`. Over a base one must assume
48	the action is `k`-linear, otherwise the action maps are not morphisms of `Under k` and the
49	diagram does not exist. `SMulCommClass G k A` says exactly `g • (r • a) = r • (g • a)`, and
50	for Milne's case it holds: `permAlgHom` is an `R`-*algebra* hom by construction, so `R`-linear
51	by `map_smul`. That instance is supplied below (`permSMulCommClass`) rather than assumed.
52	
53	## Scope
54	
55	This closes the *category* item only. Still open, and untouched here:
56	
57	* **the gluing** — `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` in `Over (Spec k̄)` for the proper curve.
58	  `SymPowColimit.lean` §6 has the availability table; the affine charts now have a carrier
59	  over the base, which is what a `Scheme.GlueData` comparison on overlaps would need, but no
60	  glue data is built here.
61	* Consequently `AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six sorries are **unchanged**, and
62	  `albanese_universal_property` still reports `sorryAx`. Nothing below is a statement about

variable {R S : CommRingCat.{u}}

namespace CommRingCat

instance : CoeSort (Under R) (Type u) where
  coe A := A.right

instance (A : Under R) : Algebra R A := RingHom.toAlgebra A.hom.hom

/-- Turn a morphism in `Under R` into an algebra homomorphism. -/
def toAlgHom {A B : Under R} (f : A ⟶ B) : A →ₐ[R] B where
  __ := f.right.hom
  commutes' a := by
    have : (A.hom ≫ f.right) a = B.hom a := by simp
    simpa only [Functor.const_obj_obj, Functor.id_obj, CommRingCat.comp_apply] using! this

@[simp]
lemma toAlgHom_id (A : Under R) : toAlgHom (𝟙 A) = AlgHom.id R A := rfl

@[simp]
lemma toAlgHom_comp {A B C : Under R} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ C) :
    toAlgHom (f ≫ g) = (toAlgHom g).comp (toAlgHom f) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma toAlgHom_apply {A B : Under R} (f : A ⟶ B) (a : A) :
    toAlgHom f a = f.right a :=
  rfl

variable (R) in
/-- Make an object of `Under R` from an `R`-algebra. -/
@[simps! hom, simps! -isSimp right]
def mkUnder (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] : Under R :=
  Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom <| algebraMap R A)

@[ext]
lemma mkUnder_ext {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] {B : Under R}
    {f g : mkUnder R A ⟶ B} (h : ∀ a : A, f.right a = g.right a) :
    f = g := by
  ext x
  exact h x

end CommRingCat

namespace AlgHom

/-- Make a morphism in `Under R` from an algebra map. -/
def toUnder {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) : CommRingCat.mkUnder R A ⟶ CommRingCat.mkUnder R B :=
  Under.homMk (CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom) <| by
    ext a
    exact f.commutes' a

@[simp]
lemma toUnder_right {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra R B] (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (a : A) :
    Under.Hom.right f.toUnder a = f a :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma toUnder_comp {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R C] (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (g : B →ₐ[R] C) :
    (g.comp f).toUnder = f.toUnder ≫ g.toUnder :=
  rfl

end AlgHom

namespace AlgEquiv

/-- Make an isomorphism in `Under R` from an algebra isomorphism. -/
def toUnder {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (f : A ≃ₐ[R] B) :
    CommRingCat.mkUnder R A ≅ CommRingCat.mkUnder R B where
  hom := f.toAlgHom.toUnder
  inv := f.symm.toAlgHom.toUnder
  hom_inv_id := by
    ext (a : (CommRingCat.mkUnder R A).right)
    simp
  inv_hom_id := by
    ext a
    simp

@[simp]
lemma toUnder_hom_right_apply {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra R B] (f : A ≃ₐ[R] B) (a : A) :
    f.toUnder.hom.right a = f a := rfl

@[simp]
lemma toUnder_inv_right_apply {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra R B] (f : A ≃ₐ[R] B) (b : B) :
    f.toUnder.inv.right b = f.symm b := rfl

@[simp]
lemma toUnder_trans {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R C] (f : A ≃ₐ[R] B) (g : B ≃ₐ[R] C) :
    (f.trans g).toUnder = f.toUnder ≪≫ g.toUnder :=
  rfl

end AlgEquiv

---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end

import Mathlib

/-!
# The tensor power **is** the `n`-ary coproduct, packaged as a `Cofan` in `Under k`

`Albanese/TensorPowerCoproduct.lean` proved the `n`-ary coproduct universal property of
`⨂[k] _ : Fin n, A` at the level of algebra homomorphisms (`existsUnique_coprodLift`),
together with both equivariance clauses. It deliberately stopped short of the categorical
crossing, and `Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`'s four-item bill therefore recorded item
3 as **partial**: the mathematics was proved, the `Cofan`/`IsColimit` packaging was not, and
`SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra` — whose diagram is built from the `n`-fold product in
`(Under k)ᵒᵖ`, i.e. the `n`-fold *coproduct* in `Under k` — consumed none of it.

This file writes that packaging. It is bookkeeping, not mathematics: every clause is one of
the algebra-level statements pushed through `AlgHom.toUnder`.

## The one trap, measured rather than guessed

`CommRingCat.toAlgHom` does **not** produce the algebra map you want out of `mkUnder k A`. It
is typed over `CommRingCat.instAlgebraCarrierRight`, i.e. `RingHom.toAlgebra (algebraMap k A)`
rebuilt from the structure morphism, not over the ambient `[Algebra k A]` instance the tensor
power is formed with. The two are equal but not syntactically the same instance, so
`toAlgHom f : ↑(mkUnder k A) →ₐ[k] ↑B` will not unify with `A →ₐ[k] ↑B`. `algHomOfMkUnderHom`
below is the version over the ambient instance; its proof is `Under.w` and one `congrArg`.

The other direction needs nothing: `AlgHom.toUnder` already lands in `mkUnder k ↑B`, and
`mkUnder k ↑B = B` holds by `rfl` for every `B : Under k`, so a lift out of the tensor power
is a morphism into `B` on the nose.

## Main results

* `algHomOfMkUnderHom` — the missing direction of the bridge (see the trap above), with
  `algHomOfMkUnderHom_toUnder` and `toUnder_algHomOfMkUnderHom` making it a bijection.
* `tensorPowerCofan` — the cofan with vertex `mkUnder k (⨂[k] _ : Fin n, A)` and coprojections
  `singleAlgHom i`.
* `tensorPowerCofanIsColimit` — **the packaging**: that cofan is a colimit. Existence is
  `coprodLift`, uniqueness is `PiTensorProduct.algHom_ext`.
* `hasCoproduct_mkUnder` — the `HasCoproduct` form, and `tensorPowerIsoCoproduct`,
  identifying `⨂[k] _ : Fin n, A` with `∐ᶜ` of `n` copies of `A` as `k`-algebras.
* `tensorPowerFanIsLimit` — the dual, in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`: the same data is the `n`-ary
  **product** there, which is the category and variance
  `SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra` works in.
* `tensorPowerCofan_inj_permAlgHom` — the equivariance, on the coprojections: permuting the
  tensor factors along `e` relabels the `i`-th coprojection to the `e⁻¹ i`-th. This is
  `permAlgHom_comp_singleAlgHom` in `Under k`, and it is what makes the identification an
  identification *of `S_n`-objects* rather than merely of objects.

## Scope — what this does and does not close

**Does**: item 3 of `StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`'s four-item bill, in full. The bill now

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct

namespace PiTensorProduct

section UnderCofan

variable (k : CommRingCat.{u}) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (n : ℕ)

/-! ## §1. The bridge, in the direction mathlib does not supply

`AlgHom.toUnder` turns an algebra map into a morphism of `Under k`. The reverse — a morphism
out of `mkUnder k A` as an algebra map over the *ambient* instance — is the one that needs
writing; see the module header for why `CommRingCat.toAlgHom` does not serve. -/

/-- **A morphism out of `mkUnder k A` as an algebra map, over the ambient instance.**

Unlike `CommRingCat.toAlgHom`, the source's `Algebra k`-structure here is the one `A` was
given, not the one rebuilt from the structure morphism of `mkUnder k A`. The `commutes'`
clause is exactly the triangle `Under.w`. -/
noncomputable def algHomOfMkUnderHom {B : Under k} (f : CommRingCat.mkUnder k A ⟶ B) :
    A →ₐ[k] B where
  __ := f.right.hom
  commutes' r :=
    congrArg (fun (g : k ⟶ B.right) => g.hom r) (f.w : (CommRingCat.mkUnder k A).hom ≫ _ = B.hom)

@[simp]
theorem algHomOfMkUnderHom_apply {B : Under k} (f : CommRingCat.mkUnder k A ⟶ B) (a : A) :
    algHomOfMkUnderHom k A f a = f.right a := rfl

/-- The bridge is a section of `AlgHom.toUnder`. -/
@[simp]
theorem algHomOfMkUnderHom_toUnder {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (f : A →ₐ[k] B) :
    algHomOfMkUnderHom k A f.toUnder = f := rfl

/-- …and a retraction of it: a morphism out of `mkUnder k A` is recovered from its algebra
map. Both directions are `rfl`, which is the point of routing through the ambient instance. -/
@[simp]
theorem toUnder_algHomOfMkUnderHom {B : Under k} (f : CommRingCat.mkUnder k A ⟶ B) :
    (algHomOfMkUnderHom k A f).toUnder = f := rfl

/-! ## §2. The cofan and its colimit property

Nothing here is new mathematics: `desc` is `coprodLift`, `fac` is
`coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom`, and `uniq` is `PiTensorProduct.algHom_ext`. -/

/-- **The cofan exhibiting `⨂[k] _ : Fin n, A` as the `n`-ary coproduct** of `n` copies of `A`
in `Under k`, with the structural inclusions `singleAlgHom i : a ↦ 1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ 1` as
coprojections. -/
noncomputable def tensorPowerCofan : Cofan (fun _ : Fin n => CommRingCat.mkUnder k A) :=
  Cofan.mk (CommRingCat.mkUnder k (⨂[k] _ : Fin n, A))
    (fun i => (singleAlgHom (R := k) (A := fun _ : Fin n => A) i).toUnder)

@[simp]
theorem tensorPowerCofan_inj (i : Fin n) :
    (tensorPowerCofan k A n).inj i
      = (singleAlgHom (R := k) (A := fun _ : Fin n => A) i).toUnder := rfl

/-- **The packaging: the tensor power is the `n`-ary coproduct in `Under k`.**

This is the statement `Albanese/TensorPowerCoproduct.lean` deliberately left to its consumer
and that `StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`'s bill recorded as the missing half of item 3. Both
clauses are the algebra-level facts pushed through the bridge of §1. -/
noncomputable def tensorPowerCofanIsColimit : IsColimit (tensorPowerCofan k A n) :=
  Cofan.IsColimit.mk _
    (fun t => (coprodLift (R := k) (A := fun _ : Fin n => A)
      (fun i => algHomOfMkUnderHom k A (t.inj i))).toUnder)
    (fun t i => by
      refine CommRingCat.mkUnder_ext (fun a => ?_)
      change (coprodLift (R := k) (A := fun _ : Fin n => A)
        (fun i => algHomOfMkUnderHom k A (t.inj i)))
          (singleAlgHom (R := k) (A := fun _ : Fin n => A) i a) = _
      rw [← AlgHom.comp_apply, coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom]
      rfl)
    (fun t m hm => by
      refine CommRingCat.mkUnder_ext (fun x => ?_)
      have h : algHomOfMkUnderHom k _ m
          = coprodLift (R := k) (A := fun _ : Fin n => A)
            (fun i => algHomOfMkUnderHom k A (t.inj i)) := by
        refine algHom_ext (fun i => ?_)
        ext a
        rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, coprodLift_comp_singleAlgHom]
        exact congrArg (fun (g : CommRingCat.mkUnder k A ⟶ t.pt) => g.right a) (hm i)
      exact congrArg (fun (g : (⨂[k] _ : Fin n, A) →ₐ[k] t.pt) => g x) h)

/-- The `HasCoproduct` form. -/
theorem hasCoproduct_mkUnder : HasCoproduct (fun _ : Fin n => CommRingCat.mkUnder k A) :=
  ⟨⟨⟨tensorPowerCofan k A n, tensorPowerCofanIsColimit k A n⟩⟩⟩

/-- **The identification of objects**: `⨂[k] _ : Fin n, A` is `∐ᶜ` of `n` copies of `A`, as an
object of `Under k`. -/
noncomputable def tensorPowerIsoCoproduct
    [HasCoproduct (fun _ : Fin n => CommRingCat.mkUnder k A)] :
    CommRingCat.mkUnder k (⨂[k] _ : Fin n, A)
      ≅ ∐ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => CommRingCat.mkUnder k A) :=
  (tensorPowerCofanIsColimit k A n).coconePointUniqueUpToIso (colimit.isColimit _)

/-! ## §3. Dually, in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`: the same data is the `n`-ary **product**

`SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra` works in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ` and forms `∏ᶜ` there. Under
`op` that product is this coproduct, so the fan below is the object its `permDiagram` is built
on. -/

/-- **The tensor power as the `n`-ary product in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`** — the category and variance
`SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra` works in. -/
noncomputable def tensorPowerFanIsLimit :
    IsLimit (tensorPowerCofan k A n).op :=
  (tensorPowerCofanIsColimit k A n).op

/-- The `HasProduct` form in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`. -/
theorem hasProduct_op_mkUnder :
    HasProduct (fun i : Fin n => Opposite.op ((fun _ : Fin n => CommRingCat.mkUnder k A) i)) :=
  ⟨⟨⟨(tensorPowerCofan k A n).op, tensorPowerFanIsLimit k A n⟩⟩⟩

/-! ## §4. The equivariance, on the coprojections

An identification of objects licenses nothing about symmetric powers; the actions must match.
At the level of a cofan the action is visible on the coprojections, and the statement is
`TensorPowerCoproduct.permAlgHom_comp_singleAlgHom` in `Under k`.

**Read the `e⁻¹`.** `permAlgHom e` sends `tprod x` to `tprod (x ∘ e)`, so the tuple with `a` in
slot `i` is hit at the slot `j` with `e j = i`. The inversion is the same convention
`SymPowTensorAction.permAlgHom_comp`, `SymPowColimit.permEnd` and
`SymPowInvariantsUnder.invEquivalence_comp_op_map` each carry. -/

/-- **The comparison respects the `S_n`-actions, at the coprojections.**

`inj i ≫ permAlgHom e = inj (e⁻¹ i)`: permuting the tensor factors along `e` relabels the
`i`-th coprojection to the `e⁻¹ i`-th. -/
theorem tensorPowerCofan_inj_permAlgHom (e : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) :
    (tensorPowerCofan k A n).inj i ≫ (permAlgHom (k : Type u) A e).toUnder
      = (tensorPowerCofan k A n).inj (e.symm i) := by
  refine CommRingCat.mkUnder_ext (fun a => ?_)
  exact congrArg (fun (g : A →ₐ[k] (⨂[k] _ : Fin n, A)) => g a)
    (permAlgHom_comp_singleAlgHom (R := k) (A' := A) e i)

end UnderCofan

end PiTensorProduct

To kernel-check one or a few Lean modules when a shared `lake` mutex is held by another lane
(AJCR's is `/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock`, a mkdir DIRECTORY lock), do **not** queue a
`lake build`. Write oleans into a scratch tree instead — it touches no shared build state, so the
protocol's lock does not apply (concurrent-lane protocol §5b explicitly permits the narrowest
check):

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/scratch-oleans
REAL=.lake/build/lib/lean
# seed the scratch root with SYMLINKS to every existing olean
for o in $(cd $REAL && find <RootModuleDir> -name '*.olean'); do
  mkdir -p /tmp/scratch-oleans/$(dirname $o)
  ln -s "$(realpath $REAL/$o)" "/tmp/scratch-oleans/$o"
done
LP=$(lake env printenv LEAN_PATH)
export LEAN_PATH="/tmp/scratch-oleans:$LP"
lean -o /tmp/scratch-oleans/<Path>/<Mod>.olean <Path>/<Mod>.lean; echo "EXIT=$?"
```

Three traps, all hit on the first attempt:

- **`lake env lean` overwrites your `LEAN_PATH`.** Use plain `lean` after exporting it, or the
  scratch root is silently dropped and you get "object file ... does not exist".
- **Lean resolves each module against the FIRST matching root only**, so an unseeded scratch root
  makes every already-built dependency look absent. Hence the symlink seeding — cheap, no copying.
- Build the chain in dependency order and write each module's olean into the scratch root, so the
  next module in the chain can find it.

Cost measured 2026-07-29: ~18 s per module, against a `lake build` of the same target that had
previously burned 3300 s and hit its timeout under 8-lane contention.

**Why it is worth doing rather than deferring.** Applied to four modules a predecessor had
committed unverified, it found **two real proof errors** that no sorry census, job count or
`git ls-tree` readback could see — see [[binder-hides-work-from-a-sorry-census]] and
[[rfl-equal-spellings-block-rw]] for the two shapes. A module can be sorry-free, rooted, and red.

Limitation to state honestly in a report: this checks the named modules against *existing* oleans
for their dependencies. It is a faithful kernel check of those files, but it is not evidence that
the whole project builds, and it will not notice that a dependency's olean is stale — cross-check
olean mtimes against sources when that matters ([[measure-absence-at-the-root]] is the related
trap for absence claims).
